chunk-j-k1-11-kartapi-kalpita-v10.speaker: Utpaladeva's pūrvapakṣin (Buddhist objector voice), reported by Abhinavagupta
chunk-j-k1-11-kartapi-kalpita-v10.question: Given that action, object and determination all fail, and the relation itself is refuted, what becomes of the agent?
premises: A fourfold absence is consolidated as the reason: absence of action, of the other, of the relation, and of the determination of their being (abhāvacatuṣṭaya, hetutā via tena).
The relation cannot stand: what rests on two cannot be one (dviṣṭhasyānekatvāt); the established expects nothing further (siddhasyānyānapekṣaṇāt); dependence is unfitting (pāratantryādyayogāt).
Refutation works by determined non-being with place-time restriction (here, now, no jar) — not by bare non-perception; universal absence needs a prameya-grounded contradiction (tadrūpadvayavirodha).
The general-characteristic refuter: two simultaneous own-form completions cannot be one (two jars in two houses); ekatva is non-distinct form.

Expectation (apekṣā) cannot save the relation: in the inert it is unfit; the rājñaḥ puruṣa example shows the genitive marks dependence, not a real relation; mutual expectation collapses into word-only unity.
Therefore the agent too is constructed (tena kartāpi kalpitaḥ): the pūrvapakṣa closes, to be reversed by the siddhānta (the agent as the real, free self).
chunk-j-k1-11-kartapi-kalpita-v10.inference: Since relation is impossible in every proposed form (dependence, expectation, adhesion, word), and refutation is secured by determined non-being, the agent — like action and object before it — is only imagined.
uncertainties: dviṣṭhasyānekarūpatvāt: the two-resting many-form crux kept as Abhinavagupta states it.
sārvātrikī asattā via tadrūpadvayavirodha: Abhinavagupta’s own move, kept close.
Print dash-runs (3 spots, L0 AMBIGUOUS): extent of loss unknown, never reconstructed.
saṃśca opening quotation (L0 AMBIGUOUS): unresolvable from T1/pilot; left open.

chunk-v2-n-sastho-k8-11-v28.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator voice)
chunk-v2-n-sastho-k8-11-v28.question:
The ṣaṣṭho vimarśa (the apohanaśakti) closes. Its final concern: the inner appearance
(antarābhāsa) stands firm in memory, construction, and cognition alike (kārikā 8); it is innate in the
cognition whose form is the external manifestation, while it stands in memory etc. (kārikā 9); it is
innate in the freely-wandering construction (kārikā 10); and hence, from the manifestation of the
uplifting as wished, knowledge and action are clear for every living one (kārikā 11). Along the way,
the freed souls (muktāṇava) and the mantreśvaras are discussed.
premises:
Even in the mokṣa-state, the freed atoms (muktāṇava) — from the parama-śiva, from the
ādi-śiva-ness, from the stain-removal-manifested-śiva-ness — have a distinction. By this part, in the
duality-side, the freed atoms are indeed distinct, and their manifestation, by the śiva-ness, is the
un-broken all-knowing; but the three-time-manifestation, being established in the māyīya-knower's
manifestation, does not fail to flash for them either (from their all-knowing). The 'ca' says: the
mantreśvaras, by the authority's exhaustion, even in the mokṣa, in that place, of the other — the atom's
word-obtaining-cause, the dīkṣā, the vow, the japa, the tapas, the samādhāna, the caryā — by the

chunk-v2-q-saptamo-k11-close-v31.question:
The saptamo vimarśa closes with the question of the *omniscient* (sarvajña) — the
supreme knower who is the support of all the powers. The Buddhist objector presses: if the piśāca (the
goblin) is not perceived even by the omniscient, how can he deny it? The analysis turns on whether the
omniscient's non-perception of the piśāca establishes its non-being, and how the ordinary knower
(arvāgdarśana) differs. This grounds the omniscient as the one who knows all — the support of the
powers.
premises:
Even if the piśāca is not seen by us, the form-and-the-rest atoms are there — not seen by us, but seen
by the omniscient. The atoms have no un-precedented variety. The "na tathā" — the obstructing ones
also, not utterly. The "dūrataram" — the shadow, made by the darkness, with the interval, the
distinguished, the same-class-devoid interval; the middle-darkness or the middle-void. In their own
place, they withdraw; by the unable-moment-production-order, they are withdrawn. Hence the
piśāca-atoms are, for the omniscient, equal to the darkness-and-the-rest-other-being-atoms. But if the
piśāca is absent, then where the piśāca had occupied the interval, the āloka-atoms alone, being seen,
are the object of the piśāca's-absence-dealing for the omniscient. The objection: "seeing the other
objects, how does the omniscient deny the distinct piśāca?" — in the piśāca's being-or-not-being, the
own-form-standing of these is not lost; the distinct-piśāca's-absence is, by this way, hard to
establish even by the omniscient. The "athavā" (or): whatever is, is to be seen by him; then, there, if
he does not see the piśāca, it is not — and there, everything is the piśāca-included thing, known by
another cognition distinct from its being; or that very cognition is the object of the
piśāca's-absence-dealing — so the interval-atom-tracing does nothing. The objection "why is it not so
for us too?" — answered (arvāk): "he who sees the limited, for him there is no known" — this
cognition arises, by which the cognition is the cause of the being-included-cognition-marker
non-being-dealing. But where the certainty arises (like the smelling, the tasting, the attending, the
touching — the necessary-conceiving of the smell-cognition), there the smell-cognition's removal is
the cause of the non-being-dealing (the breath-entering-cognition-marker, the un-divided-from-the-
smell-taste-sound-touch-absence). Hence, though the piśāca's-absence is grasped by him who grasps the
āloka or the place (by the piśāca's otherness), still it is the limited, grasped as if un-grasped (no
cause of the removal of the conceiving of the distinct in the place or the āloka). The objection "if
the piśāca's non-negatability's cause is the invisibility, then the jar's negatability's cause would
be the visibility (1.7.10, the 'svajñāna-maghaṭātmatā')" — answered (siddham): "every negation
culminates in the identity-negation; and there the visibility is un-deviating (the hetubindu: the
distinction is to be said)."
chunk-v2-q-saptamo-k11-close-v31.inference:
Decision for L2
Proceed. The argument is understood: the omniscient, seeing all the atoms, knows the piśāca's absence
in its place (the āloka-atoms alone); the limited seer (arvāk) cannot — his non-perception is only the
limited, not the established non-being; and every negation culminates in the identity-negation, where
the visibility is un-deviating. The omniscient is the support of all the powers — the one who knows all,
whose non-perception establishes, whose perception is whole. The ||7|| colophon closes the saptamo
vimarśa.

chunk-j-k1-11-kartapi-kalpita-v10.plain_english:
**"Thence the agent too is constructed"**

The Buddhist's attack has been relentless. He has denied the self, denied the cognition, denied the
action. Now he completes it. For what holds all these together — the *relation* between the knower and
the known, between the agent and the act — is itself impossible; and once the relation is gone, "thence
the agent too is constructed." The agent, like everything else, is only a fabrication, a convenient
construction with nothing real behind it.

The kārikā's "thence" gathers a fourfold absence as its reason: the absence of the action, the absence
of the object, the absence of the relation, and the absence of any determination of being in any of
them. And the relation's absence is argued on its own terms. A relation would have to stand *in both*
its terms — in the knower and the known at once. But the two-resting thing cannot be one: what stands
in two cannot be a single thing, any more than the two jars in the two houses are one jar. Moreover,
the established does not expect another — a thing already complete does not reach out for a relation —
and the dependence that a relation would impose is itself unfitting. So the relation is absent; and
with it, the agent that the relation would bind together is only constructed.

Abhinavagupta pauses to make one methodological point, and it is important. The Buddhist thinks he
refutes the relation by a bare non-perception — "I do not see it, so it is not." But a bare
non-perception proves non-being only within a restriction of place and time: "here, now, there is no
jar." It cannot reach the universal non-being of the relation. To do that, one must show a real
contradiction in the opponent's own account — that the very form he ascribes to the relation is
contradicted by another form he ascribes to it. That is a refutation grounded in the thing itself
(prameya-niṣṭha), not a mere failure to perceive.

And this is where the pūrvapakṣa — the no-self attack — comes to its close. The Buddhist has shown,
to his own satisfaction, that the self, the cognition, the action, and the relation all fall; and
"thence the agent too is constructed." The whole edifice of a real knower and doer is, for him, a
fabrication.

**The inner appearance stands firm — for every living one**

The ṣaṣṭho vimarśa, on the power of removal, comes to its close; and its final claim is one of
unfailing constancy. The inner appearance — the self-grasp, the reflexive-awareness — stands firm in
memory, in construction, and in cognition alike (kārikā 8). It is not something that flickers in and
out, present in cognition and absent in memory. It is the one light that runs through them all. In the
cognition whose form is the external manifestation, this inner appearance — the prior-experience-form —
is innate (kārikā 9); and it stands, too, in memory and the rest. In the freely-wandering construction,
the inner appearance is innate indeed (kārikā 10): the construction may wander at will, forming this or
that shape, but the self-grasp that shapes it is always there, in the mind's range. And hence — from the
manifestation of the uplifting as wished — knowledge and action are clear, established for every living
one (kārikā 11).

And this constancy extends even to the freed. Even in liberation, the freed souls (muktāṇava) are
distinct — yet their manifestation, by the śiva-ness, is the un-broken all-knowing. The three-time
manifestation may be established in the māyīya knower, but it does not fail to flash for them either,
from their all-knowing. And the mantreśvaras — even in liberation, by the exhaustion of their authority,
in the place of the other — by the word-obtaining (the dīkṣā, the vow, the japa, the tapas, the
concentration, the conduct), transmigrating, are all-knowing; the knower-ness is not de-valued. The
animal-atoms are distinct only in their animal-ness, generally. The categories, the worlds, the
elements, the kalā, the mantra, the word, the phoneme — the jars and the rest, with respect to their
own class, are not utterly unprecedented.

The objection "how, in the dealing-time, is the creation?" is met. The creation is by the unity — at
that time, per-knower, the jar-appearance and the body-appearance are distinct, but the consciousness-
self alone [creates them]; and the knower-distinction is not destroyed, for it stands in the
prāṇa-puryaṣṭaka and the like. And the appearance is the cognition: the jar-form appearance, though
known, is of the knower-operation-form, of the knower-standing-ness — it is the cognition itself. The
final objection — "then by the knower's will, per-moment the creation and withdrawal of objects and
knowers — how does the maheśvara shine?" — is answered: the order-word's pure-form-sequence is not the
whole; the maheśvara, the Lord, is the one who shines through it all.

So the vimarśa closes with the constancy of the self-grasp. It is innate in memory, in cognition, in
construction; it stands firm for the bound and for the freed, for the animal-atom and the mantreśvara;
and from its manifestation — the uplifting as wished — knowledge and action are clear for every living
one. The inner appearance, the reflexive-awareness, never fails: it is the very nature of the light,
and it is what makes every living one a knower and a doer. The apohanaśaktivimarśa — the reflexion on
the power of removal — here comes to its close.

  kārikā 10 (the innate in the freely-wandering construction); kārikā 11 (the uplifting-as-wished,
  knowledge and action clear for every living one); the muktāṇava distinct yet all-knowing; the
  three-time manifestation; the mantreśvara (the word-obtaining, the dīkṣā etc., the transmigration,
  the all-knowing); the paśvaṇūṇa; the tattvabhuvanādayaḥ; the jars not utterly unprecedented; the
  "not then-created and then-withdrawn"; the prior-created-ness; the creation by the unity; the
  knower-distinction not destroyed (the prāṇa-puryaṣṭaka); the appearance as the cognition (the

**The omniscient knows all — and his non-perception establishes**

The saptamo vimarśa, on the one support of the powers, closes with the figure of the omniscient — the
supreme knower who is the support. And the question that tests him is the goblin, the piśāca. Suppose
there is a piśāca in the dark interval. We do not see it; but the atoms of form and the rest are there,
unseen by us, seen by the omniscient. The piśāca's atoms, for the omniscient, are no different from the
atoms of the darkness and the other beings — he sees them all. If the piśāca is truly absent, then where
it might have stood, the omniscient sees only the atoms of light (āloka), and these — being seen — are
the very ground of his dealing "there is no piśāca here."

But the objector presses: "seeing all the other objects, how does the omniscient deny a *distinct*
piśāca?" The answer is subtle. Whatever is, the omniscient sees it; so if, in that place, he does not
see the piśāca, then it is not there. Everything in that place is the piśāca-included thing — the whole
known together — and its being or not-being is decided by his seeing. The distinct-piśāca's-absence is
established by the omniscient's whole, un-broken perception, not by any tracing of the interval's
atoms.

And why is this not so for us? Because we see only the limited (arvāk). For one who sees the limited,
there is no such un-broken knowledge: his non-perception of the piśāca is only the limited — the
grasped-as-if-un-grasped — not the established non-being. There is no cause, in his limited seeing, to
remove the conceiving of the distinct thing in that place. The omniscient's non-perception, by contrast,
establishes; the limited seer's does not.

The final objection: "if the piśāca's non-negatability is caused by its invisibility, then the jar's
negatability should be caused by its visibility." But this fails: every negation, Abhinavagupta says,
culminates in the identity-negation — and there the visibility is un-deviating. The jar's negation
rests on its identity being negated in that place, and the seeing that grounds it is whole. The
omniscient's seeing is not the limited seeing of the ordinary; it is the whole, un-broken perception of
the one who knows all.

So the vimarśa closes on the omniscient as the support of the powers. He sees all the atoms, all the
beings, all the interval — and his perception, being whole, establishes what is and what is not. The
limited seer, the arvāgdarśana, sees only a part; the omniscient sees the whole. And this omniscient —
the one whose perception is un-broken, whose non-perception establishes, whose support is all the
powers — is the maheśvara, the one knower in whom all the powers rest. With his establishment, the
seventh vimarśa — the reflexion on the one support of the powers — comes to its close.

- **Preserved:** the piśāca/āloka-atom analysis; the atoms unseen by us, seen by the omniscient; the
  atoms' no-un-precedented-variety; the shadow/darkness/interval; the withdrawal in their own place;

chunk-v2-s-astamo-close-jnanadhikara-v33.plain_english:
**The knowers are one, and the one is the Lord**

The jñānādhikāra — the whole first adhikāra of the Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī — comes to its
close. And it closes, fittingly, on the unity. It was said at the start that the one is the maheśvara;
now the unity is established. Kārikā 10: without that unity, the world-path of the consciousnesses
would not be; from the manifestation-unity, that one-ness, that one alone is the knower, it is
established.

The argument is simple and decisive. The whole dealing of the world — the path by which consciousnesses
know, remember, and act together — would be impossible if the consciousnesses were a scattered crowd of
mutually opaque streams. But the dealing is; so the consciousnesses must be one. And this is not hard to
accept, for the manifestation (prakāśa) is the very essence of the consciousnesses, and the
manifestation is one — there is no difference in the light itself. That one manifestation is, in truth,
the knower. The one light that shines in all the consciousnesses is the one knower, the param-essence
knower, the paramātman. Even the Sāṃkhya's and the Jaiminīya's self-luminous consciousness, and the
ancient Vaiśeṣika's consciousness-nature self, all point to this one.

The objection comes: "each cognition rests, in its own self-experience, in its own joining — what is
new here?" And the answer is that the known itself — the blue and the rest — has the manifestation as
its param-essence; the blue is, in its being, the light. So the unity is real, not a construction. And
the apparent difference of the known is made only by the māyā-power: the known-marker part, made
distinct from the manifestation as if it were other, is still the manifestation's own part. The
difference is the māyā's making; the unity is the truth.

And the Sāṃkhya's puruṣa — the separate self it posits — is not another at all. It is the un-recognized
own-lordship, the contracted consciousness; its knowledge and action, dealt as "I," are the
"I"-recollection. And this "I"-recollection, Abhinavagupta notes, is the pervader of all the states —
the pure, the mixed, the un-pure — gathered, not abandoned. The threefold self-recognition runs through
them all.

Then kārikā 11 sums up the whole: he alone, by the fixed reflexive-awareness-ness, is the great Lord;
the reflexive-awareness alone, of the God, in the pure knowledge-action, since. The great-Lordship is
nothing but the reflexive-awareness — the one who is aware of himself, fixedly, is the Lord; and that
reflexive-awareness is the God's own pure knowledge-and-action. The great-Lordship is not an added
power; it is the self-awareness itself, the "I" that knows and acts, the one knower.

And so the jñānādhikāra — the adhikāra on knowledge — is complete. The ||8|| colophon closes the
vimarśa on the great-Lordship in the one-support of the powers; and the great colophon reads:
"completed — this, the first jñānādhikāra." The first of the four adhikāras of the IPVV is done. It
has established the self, the powers, the one knower, the great-Lordship — all culminating in the
unity: the one manifestation is the one knower, and the one knower, aware of himself, is the Lord.

chunk-v3-p-tattva-caturtho-close-k1-3-v4.plain_english:
**The closing sum: the recognition, and the end of the whole teaching**

We come to the end. This final vimarśa of the Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī is the closing sum — the
drawing together of everything that has gone before. And its theme is fittingly the *transmission* of
the teaching itself: it comes from the guru, from the śāstra, and from the self.

The whole teaching — the self-manifest essence, established by the knowledge and the action, aided by
reason — has been given. Part of it comes from the self (svataḥ); part from the śāstra (śāstrataḥ);
and part must come from the guru (gurutaḥ). For even the vision of the śāstra must be carried to its
proper power by the lineage of teachers. And here Abhinavagupta is stern: "the book-studied knowledges,
without the guru-order," he warns, "practicing and teaching, ripen long in hell." The teaching must be
received from the living line — from the ādi-Śrīkaṇṭhanātha down through Durvāsa and Tryambakāditya, the
mental sons who carry the un-precedented, effort-less word.

And now the path itself. Abhinavagupta presents it as a "new, well-fitted path," spoken by the great
gurus in the Śivadṛṣṭi. It is the path of the recognition. Since liberation is from the recognition
alone, all the elaborate effort-yogas are useless here; this is the clear means, effort-less,
un-undertaken, yet bearing the great fruit. The breath-controls and the rest are artificial; the
un-made reality does not yield to a sixteenth part of such effort. Even the proud fancies of the bound
— "I am the king," "I have slain my enemy" — are, when examined, still other-dependent, riding on the
Lord's power. The recognition cuts through all of it. And its fruit is the while-living-liberated, the
jīvanmukta: the one who, even in the body, is already free, and who at the fall of the body is simply
the supreme Lord. This, Abhinavagupta says, is the most wondrous thing of all — liberation in this very
life.

The closing sum puts it in a beautiful image. The lover stands near, sought by the slender woman; but
as long as he is not recognized, he cannot be enjoyed. So the world-Lord — always present, always near —
is not experienced in his own splendor until the recognition arises. The world has him before it, and
yet does not see him, until the single act of recognition turns the un-known nearness into the joy of
union. One who knows only the mere flash of recognition gains the bliss; one who cultivates it gains
the thousand-fold embrace.

And this recognition, Abhinavagupta reminds us, was established for the world by Utpala — "the sun-rise
son" — for the effort-less establishment of all people, not by caste or conduct but by the very fact of
being born a knower. Through it, all beings are graced; and by it, the author himself is complete. The
whole teaching — the Lord's recognition — is here gathered and handed on.

The closing vimarśa then turns to the author's own lineage — the vivṛtikāra's seventeen verses of
praise. They trace the line: Varāha-gupta, the Cukhulaka, father of Bhūtirāja; Bhūtirāja himself;
Haṭitalakṣmaṇagupta, the maker of the śāstra, the guru of Abhinava; the Tryambaka with its three
powers; and the method of the recognition throughout. The final verses praise the supreme Lord and
hand the work to him: "the Lord-recognition, from the reflective-awareness of the Lord, may he make it
the one minding the self's reflection." And then the two colophons close the entire work: the
"all-conclusion, the fourth vimarśa"; and "completed — this, the Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī, the
composition of the Abhinavagupta-foots, whose fame is won by meditation on the feet of Tri-nayana."

So ends the greatest work of Abhinavagupta — the Vivṛtivimarśinī on the recognition of the Lord. It
has traced, across four adhikāras, the knowledge and the action of consciousness, the categories of
the world, the knowers and the stains, the bond and the liberation. And it closes where it began: the
own-self of all beings is the one Lord, and the recognition of this — received from the guru, the
śāstra, and the self — is the whole of liberation. The book ends, and the recognition begins.

essence: The antagonist completes the no-self offensive by moving from things to their togetherness: where nothing genuinely relates, no one genuinely acts.
Relation is tried in every candidate shape — resting in both terms at once, expectation, adhesion, mere wording — and each shape breaks on the ground that what rests on two cannot be one.

Refutation itself gets its method fixed: not bare not-seeing, but a pointed-out impossibility inside the opponent's own admissions, holding only here-and-now unless the contradiction is made universal.
With knower, known, act and bond all set aside as built, the doer stands exposed as built too — the exact spot where the recognition teaching will later reverse the verdict.

Even in the mokṣa-state, the freed atoms (muktāṇava) — from the parama-śiva, from the
ādi-śiva-ness, from the stain-removal-manifested-śiva-ness — have a distinction.

The saptamo vimarśa closes with the question of the *omniscient* (sarvajña) — the
supreme knower who is the support of all the powers.

Even if the piśāca is not seen by us, the form-and-the-rest atoms are there — not seen by us, but seen
by the omniscient.
The book of knowledge closes by proving its knowers are one: no shared world-path without one light, and the light itself admits no difference.
Every rival witness is conscripted rather than refuted — Sāṃkhya, Mīmāṃsā, Vaiśeṣika all point, unwittingly, at the same self-luminous one.
Objections about difference, error and mutual expectation are settled inside the unity: māyā arranges the many without ever leaving the one.
Lordship turns out to need no addition: fixed self-awareness just is the great Lord, closing the adhikāra where it began — with the one.
The book closes by naming its own delivery system: part from the self, part from the śāstra, and part only from the guru — book-learning alone is mocked.
The path it delivers is one and effortless: the recognition itself, well-fitted and new, needing no yogic hardship to liberate the living.
Objections from every school are gathered, not dodged — each is shown a seat inside the recognition, and the teaching stands complete.
Lineage praised, colophons set down: the whole teaching hands itself to the Lord — one recognition, transmitted.

jñānāntareṇa vedyam, yadivā tadeva jñānaṃ tasya piśācābhāvavyavahāraviṣayaḥ iti na antarālavartiparamāṇvantarānusaraṇena kiñcit nanu asmadāderapi evaṃ kasmāt na bhavati ucyate arvāk iti parimitaṃ yaḥ paśyati, tasya na jñeyamasti,- ityevaṃ jñānamutpadyate yena jñānameva sahitajñānalakṣaṇamabhāvavyavahṛterhetuḥ yatra tu utpadyate iti niścayo jighrata iva rasayata iva avadadhata iva spṛśata iva gandhādijñānāvaśyakasaṃbhāvanāt, tatra gandhādijñānanivṛttireva śvāsapraveśanajñānādirūpāvyatiriktagandharasaśabdasparśābhāva- vyavahārahetureva tato yadyapi amunā ālokaṃ pradeśameva vā gṛhṇatā piśācābhāvo gṛhītaḥ piśācānyatvāt tayoḥ, tathāpi prādeśiko'sau gṛhīto'pi agṛhītakalpaḥ pradeśe āloke vā bhinnasya asya saṃbhāvanānivṛttikāraṇābhāvādetāvati [vatī bahubhiḥ prakārairapi ukte vastuni nanu yadi piśācasya aniṣedhyatāyāmadṛśyatā hetuḥ, tarhi ghaṭāderniṣedhyatāyāṃ ............................ṣvajñānamaghaṭātmatām ityādyuddeśeṣu dṛśyatā hetutvena nirdeśyā na,- ityāha siddham iti ya aniṣedhyatvamanubadhnāti adṛśyatve'pi iti yadi ālokaḥ paramāṇuśo dṛśyo bhavet, tadā paramāṇuṃ paramāṇuṃ gaṇayato nirantaratvena bhavet buddhiratra sthāne yaḥ piśācaparamāṇuḥ saṃbhāvyate, tadvilakṣaṇo'yamālokaparamāṇureva piśācaparamāṇvabhāvasvabhāvaḥ, paramāṇvantare'pi evamiti piśācaparamāṇavaḥ śakyeran pradeśe ghaṭavat nirākartumālokaparamāṇūnāmeva tatra piśācaparamāṇvabhāvatvāt, natu paramāṇuśo darśanamasti sthūlaikaghanavitatapratibhāsāt tanmadhye ca parimitatimirādiparamāṇuvat [paramāṇuvarapiśāca piśācaparamāṇūnāmapi śaṅkanīyatvāt evamālokasya paramāṇuśo dṛśyatve syāt piśācābhāvasiddhirarvāgdarśanasyāpi,- ityuktamapi yāvadgati vicāryam [vicāramātraṃ natu etat sthitamartharūpamityāha athavā iti paramāṇuśo'dṛśyatve'pi yadi nairantaryapratighātakāḥ piśācaparamāṇavaḥ saṃbhāvyeran, tat sāntaratvābhāve bhavet tanniṣedho, natu evam rasagandhasparśaparamāṇavo hi yathaiva adṛśyatvena santo'pi na ekaghanarūpapratyayaṃ nighnanti, tathā paiśācāḥ paramāṇavo rūpamayā api asmadādicakṣuragocarā eva atasteṣāmantarālarūpāṇāmagrahaṇenaiva asaṃhatatvaṃ gṛhyate yathā, tathā pradarśitaṃ vitatya bāhyārthasiddhāvupādhyāyadharmottareṇa pradeśamadhye'pi piśācaniṣedhasya aśakyatā itthameva anusaraṇīyā tataśca yathā bhūtalasya antar ityapi sautramanusṛtaṃ bhavati sarvathā ityapi vyākhyātaṃ bhavati iyatāpica yāvadgativicāreṇa sarvathāśabdaḥ sautro vyākhyātaḥ iti upasaṃharati tataśca iti prāsaṅgikadoṣapraśamanaparamidaṃ sūtraṃ pūrvasūtrārthasya avicalatāmādhātumiti tadeva anusandhatte avaśyaṃ ca iti ayameva iti ...............ālokacayo'ndhasya sparśo vā............... itiprastāvena tādātmyābhāvo ya uktaḥ yatsaṃvedanam iti yasya jñānasya saṃvedanaṃ bhūtalasaṃvedanasthānīyam tasya iti jñānasya bhūtalasya iva grāhakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ bhavet yena rūpajñānābhāvaḥ pratyakṣataḥ sidhyediti vyavahriyate, tat tādṛśaṃ vijñānaṃ na kiñcidasti, - iti yāvat nanu sparśajñānasya yat pratyakṣaṃ svasaṃvedanaṃ, tena yata ekameva sparśajñānaṃ gṛhītaṃ, na rūpajñānaṃ; tataḥ kevalabhūtalajñānatulyādekajñānasaṃsargayogyajñānāntaraniṣedhaḥ syāt syāt satyaṃ, yadi rūpajñāne bhavatyapi tadeva sparśajñānasvasaṃvedanaṃ rūpajñānasvasaṃvedanākārāntaraṃ bibhṛyāt; natu evaṃ svapne'pi,- iti nirūpyate nahi iti ghaṭetyādivaidharmyāśayena atra hetumāha jñānadvitva iti tasya saṃvedanasya jñānasvarūpagrāhakasya ekatvaṃ na upapadyate nanu vedyabhūte cet dve jñāne [dvaitajñāne ghaṭabhūtalatulye, tat kimāyātaṃ tatsaṃvedanasya āha-jñānasvarūpāt vijñeyalakṣaṇāt tasya abhedaḥ atrāpi hetuḥ svasaṃvedanatvameva evamekajñānasaṃsargasya samastābhāvavyavahāravyāptyabhāvaṃ pradarśya arthasya nyāyasya vyāpakatvaṃ darśayati ukta iti turviśeṣadyotakaḥ tatsattaiva iti niyamavatī rūpajñānasattā vyavacchinne svasaṃvedane nirbhāsamānā rūpajñānābhāvavyavahārāspadam nanu iyatā sparśajñānatādātmyāpannaṃ rūpajñānaṃ kāmaṃ niṣiddhaṃ, tatsamaye tu dvitīyasya vyatiriktasyaiva rūpajñānasya kathamabhāvaḥ sidhyati ucyate kāryābhāvāt iti rūpajñānaṃ yadi bhavet sparśajñānāvasare, tat sparśajñānāt yo jāyate vikalpaḥ, sa rūpajñānādapi jātaḥ iti rūpasparśobhayavikalpanavyāpāraṃ vikalpajñānaṃ svasaṃvedyaṃ bhavet, naca tat tathābhūtamastīti atraiva dṛṣṭāntamāha pradīpe'pi iti yathā pūrvaṃ rūpadarśanāt pratighātakāraṇānāpātācca niścitasvanetrasadbhāvo'ndhakāre pradīpābhāvaṃ rūpajñānasya kāryasya abhāvāt niścinoti, tathā viśiṣṭavikalpātmakakāryābhāvāt rūpajñānasya abhāvādamunaiva nyāyena sahitatvarahitatvābhāvasvarūpavāde'pi rahitāt pradeśāt kāraṇasya ghaṭasya abhāva iti anumānataiva bhavet, natu sa eva sa ityalaṃ bahunā etāvat iti natu eṣāmanyā gatirvahatīti yāvacchakti vimṛṣṭaṃ paradarśanamiti vadan vikalpo'pi pṛthageva astu svasaṃviditaḥ ityādidūṣaṇāntarasaṃbhāvanamatrāpi syāt,- iti darśayan ekasaṃvedanābhyupagamena idamapi na kiñcit,- iti sūcayati tata eva āha yuktaṃ tu ityādinā anena śabdarasagandhānāmabhāvo'pi samagrasāmagrīkatve'pi siddhe jñānātmakakāryābhāvena samarthitaḥ, tajjñānābhāvaśca tatsvasaṃvedanābhāvena, antarnādakāyasparśadantodakarasatripuṭikāgandhasaṃvedanena tu kāmaṃ bāhyaśabdādinirāso bhavet, ākāśadhāraṇāsamāpannasya tu samastatadabhāvavedanaṃ kathaṃ samastaśabdādyabhāve yoginastadā niścetavye nāsti avakāśaḥ ekajñānasaṃsargayogyavastudvayānyatara- niyatavijñānāvaseyatāsamarthanasya,- ityalaṃ bahunā nanu evaṃ bhavatprasādhitenaiva nyāyena pramāṇabhūtaśuktikā- rajatābhāvānyatarajñānaprāmāṇyasaṃvedanameva tadanyarajatajñānaprāmāṇyābhāvajñānaṃ siddhameva satyaṃ siddhaṃ, tathāpitu sādhyaṃ na siddhamiti darśayati sūtreṇa evaṃ rupyavidābhāvarūpā śuktimatirbhavet na tvādyarajatajñapteḥ syādaprāmāṇyavedikā anena hi śuktikājñānasya na idaṃ rajatamitijñānasya vā svarūpacintā kṛtā bhavati, natu tato vyatiriktasya ādyarajatajñānasya kiñcit khaṇḍitaṃ maṇḍitaṃ vā ghaṭajñānaprāmāṇye hi prācyapaṭabodhāprāmāṇyarūpe saṃvidite'pi prācyasya paṭabodhasya na kiñcit kṛtaṃ bhavatīti sūtrārthaḥ asadviṣayatām iti aprāmāṇyam iṣyate iti saugataiḥ tacca iti pūrvasya aprāmāṇyam etāvattu iti ayaṃ bhāvaḥ- asti tāvadeṣā pratipattirloke, sā tu kiṃpramāṇarūpā,- iti cintyam yadi pratyakṣātmikā, tadasmaddarśanameva vijayi; atha anumānātmikā, tat na upapadyate,- iti samanantarameva sūtreṇa vakṣyate nanu idamityanena tadeva avamṛśyate yatra rajatajñānamabhūt, tatraiva ca na idaṃ rajatamiti śuktikā veti jñānamuditamidānīm, naca ekamekadā rūpadvayayogi,- iti na jñānadvayaṃ pramāṇaṃ bhavitumarhatīti ānumāniko bādho bhaviṣyati tatra [atra etadeva tāvat na siddhamidamityanena tadeveti anumānaṃ ca na upapadyate asti ca bādhavyavahāraḥ, so'smannaya eva upapannaḥ,- iti sūtraṃ dharmyasiddherapi bhavedbādhā naivānumānataḥ svasaṃvedanasiddhā tu yuktā saikapramātṛjā apiśabdo bahumukhaṃ yojyaḥ anumānato'pi naiva bādhā dharmiṇo'pi hetorapica asiddheḥ naca dūrānusaraṇena iyaṃ bādhapratītiḥ, apitu svasa.vedanenaiva tataśca avaśyasamarthanīyā api ekasmiṃstu pramātari sati tasmāt svatantrāt sā jāyate,- iti sūtrārthaḥ tamavatārayati anumānamapi iti iyato'dhikaprameyatvādiyadeva avatāritam, śiṣṭaṃ tu prāktanārthanigamanameva śuktijñāna iti hetorasiddhiṃ vyācakṣāṇo dharmyasiddhiṃ tadupayoginīṃ karoti pakṣadharmatvābhidhānaprathamarūpaprasādhako hetordharmyupayogaḥ ityāśayena anyathā hetoḥ sādhyaṃ sidhyati, kiṃ tatra dharmiṇā,- iti śaṅketa kaścit hetuḥ iti aprāmāṇye rajatajñānasya sādhye nanu svarūpāsiddha eva kasmāt na ayamucyate yatra dharmyasiddhimukhaprekṣitā na ālambanīyā,- ityāśaṅkya nyāyaṃ vyutpādayati svarūpa iti iha hetusvarūpameva svarūpaṃ, na vastusvarūpaṃ yena śaśaviṣāṇaṃ svarūpāsiddhaṃ bhavet, hetośca niyatadeśakālāyogavyavacchedena sādhyasādhakatvaṃ nāma svarūpamāśrayāyattam tataśca yasya āśrayo na kaścit vākyāt pratīyate - anityaḥ śabdaścākṣuṣatvāditi, sa svarūpeṇaiva niradhiṣṭhāno bhavan na kiñcidiva sampannaḥ śabdagatasya tasya abhāvāt anyarūpādiniṣṭhatāyāśca pratītyasaṃsparśāt tato'yaṃ svarūpāsiddha ucyate śuktijñānasatyatvaṃ tu yadyapi anyatra na siddhaṃ, tathāpi svarūpeṇa bhātyeva anyanirapekṣasya tasya pratītiviśrāntipadatvāt nanu evamapi śuktikāyāṃ jñānasatyatve śuktikājñānena adhikaraṇe satyatvaṃ siddhamapi adhikaraṇāntare prakṛtarajatajñāne na siddhamiti vibhinnādhikaraṇatvena asiddhametat astu evaṃ ko doṣa ityāha vyadhikaraṇa iti kākasyetyanupātte tu svarūpāsiddha eva vā ayamiti mantavyam nanu evamāśaryāsiddhatvaṃ kasmādabhyadhāyi ucyate, sa vyadhikaraṇāsiddhasya api adhikaraṇāntarasaṃbandho na doṣāya, apitu taddvāreṇa āśrayeṇa yaḥ saṃbandhaḥ, sa eva nanu kāka eva āśrayo'stu na,- ityāha prakṛta iti svarūpeṇa iti dharmasya anyadharmyāśrayatvena dharmatayā, dharmiṇaśca anyadharmādhāratvena dharmitayā siddhāvapi satyāṃ tena dharmiṇā āśrayeṇa dharmatā, tena ca dharmeṇa āśritena tasya dharmitā,- ityevaṃ yā saṃyojanā, tasyā asiddhiryā, sā āśrayāsiddhirvā vyadhikaraṇāsiddhirvā vyapadiśyate evamasiddhasya prakāre vaicitryamuktvā prakṛte viśiṣṭamasiddhaprakāraṃ darśayati ihatu iti purā iti bādhakakāle bādhyarajatajñānāt pūrvameva śuktijñānaṃ, tadevahi rajatajñānasya smārakaṃ virodhena saṃbandheneti tadeva rajatajñānamaprāmāṇye sādhye dharmīcikirṣitam tadā iti hetvabhimataśuktikājñānasatyatāsaṃvedanakāle naiva siddham nanu na rajatajñānaṃ dharmīkariṣyate, apitu śuktikaiva etadapi na sahate tasya...ṭi tadānīmityāśayaḥ etadeva siddhasādhyatvaṃ ghaṭayati nahi iti śuktikājñānasya yo'dhunā vartate viṣayaḥ, sa rajatajñānasya prākpravṛttasya api adhunā na viṣayaḥ iti hi daivaraktāḥ kiṃśukāḥ nanu siddhasādhanaṃ kiṃnāma dūṣaṇaṃ, sādhyaṃ hi tāvat siddham, anumānasya punarastu vaiyarthyaṃ na kiñcit siddhamiti darśayati naca iti nanu yathā parvataṃ tadgataṃ ca dhūmaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāryāntaratvarayā ananumitavahnireva apakramya prasthitaḥ san smṛte adrau dharmiṇi vahnimattaṃ prācyasamayabhāvinīmadhunaiva apūrvatayā sādhayati, tathā smṛte rajate tajjñāne vā adhunaiva asattāṃ bahirapramāṇatāṃ vā sādhayet sādhayet yadi dhūmamiva hetuṃ smaret, smarecca, yadi anubhavet, naca anubhavo'sti,- ityācaṣṭe naca iti syādetat, yathā adhunā dṛśyamānāt bhittimālinyādiviśeṣāt pūrvavṛttaṃ dhūmamanu sā vahnyanumā, tayaiva satyatayā mūlasādhyayā vyāptastadgamako yo dharmo hetūcikīrṣitaḥ sa idānīṃ hetvantarādanumāyiṣyate, tataśca astyatānumānaṃ bhaviṣyati atra ucyate śuktikā iti nahi tathābhūtasādhanaṃ dharmasādhakahetvantaramasti asti hi tadā śuktiḥ, tajjñānaṃ, tatprāmāṇyaṃ, tatsvasaṃvedanaṃ ca sarvaṃ ca etat anyatra sve sve āśraye vartate iti vyadhikaraṇameva evaṃ smaryamāṇasya dharmitāmabhyupagamya dūṣaṇamuktaṃ, adhunā tāmeva na sahate rajate ca iti parvate hi smaryamāṇe vastutā asti, natu rajate, rajatajñānaṃ tu kevalamadhyavasīyate iti adhyavasite yat sādhakaṃ, tat vastubhūtaṃ jñānena kiñcit sādhitaṃ bhavati bāhyaṃ hi dṛśyaṃ vikalpyatayā adhyavasitamiti abhedādhyavasāyāt bhedānadhyavasāyāt vā vikalpena spṛṣṭamucyatām, asti [astu ca śabdārthastrividho dharmī bhāvābhāvobhayāśrayaḥ ityādibāhyābhimatapradhānādiviṣayamanumānaṃ taddharmīkartuṃ [kartuṃ natu śakyaṃ, natu evaṃ svasaṃvedanamavikalpyatvāt tasya etacca bhavadbhireva svasaṃvedanasya avikalpatāmupapādayadbhiḥ [vikalpakatāṃ aśakyasamayo hyātmā sukhādīnāmananyabhāk teṣāmataḥ svasaṃvittirnābhijalpānuṣaṅgiṇī iti vadadbhiḥ prasādhitameva nanu asti eṣā pratipattiḥ- tat rajatajñānaṃ tadeva pramāṇaṃ na abhūditi adhunaiva mayā jñāyate śuktijñānānubhavāt hetoriti bāḍhamasti, sā tu bhavanmate na kathañcit yujyate, asmanmate eva tu yujyate tadāha asmākaṃ tu iti tuśabdena yadyapi viṣayoparāgakṛtaṃ kālabhedaṃ saṃvedane'bhimanyante māyāpramātāro vedyāṃśapravaṇībhūtahṛdayatayā tata eva bhinnāni jñānāni,- iti vyavahriyate, tathāpi teṣāṃ pāramārthikaṃ rūpamabhinnameva,- iti śuktijñānasvasaṃvedanāvadhau rajatajñānasvasaṃvedanatā api māyoparāgayogāpagamāt sthitaiva māyāvidyobhayasāro hi ayaṃ vyavahāro na ekapariniṣṭhayā nirvahati tatastasya rajatajñānasya dharmiṇaḥ sādhyamapramāṇātmakamananuvṛttidharmavimarśakatvaṃ nāma yat, tat śuktikājñānasatyatayā sādhyate evaṃ parvatajñānadhūmajñānayoḥ saṃvedanīyamaprāmāṇyalakṣaṇaṃ dharmāntaraṃ yasya, tasya bhāvastena aprāmāṇyena dharmāntareṇa saṃbandhaḥ, sa eva viśeṣastasya jñānābhidhānātmā yo vyavahārastat rajatajñānamapramāṇamiti tatsādhanakāle dharmitvamupapannaṃ kālabhedenāpi sthitānāṃ rajatādijñānānāmiti saṅgatiḥ evamasmākameva idamupapannaṃ, natu bhavatāṃ kathañciditi tuśabdadyotitamupapādya prakṛtameva paraparākaraṇamanusarati naca iti lokamārgaḥ sarvo vyavahāro na bhavet, asti ca ayaṃ, tasmādavaśyaṃ saṃvidāmaikyam naca tat durupapādam prakāśa eva hi saṃvidāṃ paramārthaḥ, sa ca eko bhedābhāvāt yaśca asāvekaḥ, sa eva paramārthataḥ pramātā,- iti yadiha upadeśyaṃ, tadadhunā sthiraṃ niṣkampaṃ jātam vṛttau paramātma ityanena paramārthapramātṛtāmasya āha tathāhi ajaḍapramātṛsiddhiḥ yadyapyarthasthitiḥ............................ iti ityādināca iti ākārato bhavanmukhyo bhedaḥ, sa nāsti,-iti svarūpagrahaṇena uktam tatraiva hetuḥ cinmātrarūpatvāt iti deśakālābhyāmapi na bheda ityāha deśa iti yadyapi vicitrabhedo vyavahāra uktaḥ, tathāpi vyāpakatvāt sarvasaṅgrāhī pratipādyapratipādakabhāva iha uktaḥ, sa hi svātmani api saṃśayavitarkanirṇayādau, paratra ca upadeśakrayavikrayādau saṃbhavatyeva, tena vinā hi vyavahārasya api avyavahāryatvam nanu jñānānāṃ svasaṃvedane sve sve yojanālakṣaṇā viśrāntiriti kimetadapūrvamityāśaṅkāyāmāha yadica iti saṃvedyātmanām iti saṃvedyasya nīlāderātmabhūtānām nīlāderhi prakāśa eva yadi, tathāpi advayam tarhi bhrāntā nīlādayaḥ syuḥ atra api āha nāpi iti dvaitānāpattau hetuḥ yataḥ iti anyataḥ śarīrādervedyādeva bhedaḥ, na prakāśāt; tato'pi hi bhede bhinnaṃ bhāsitamityetadeva iti grāhyagrāhakayoḥ etacca nirṇītaṃ tanmayā dṛśyate............................... iti sūtre tathāca iti pratibimbakalpatayaiva nanu evaṃ śuktikārajatamapi pratibimbakalpamiti utsannāstribhuvane bhrāntivṛttāntāḥ satyaṃ paraprakāśāpekṣayā tarhi kva bhrāntivyavahāraḥ āha māyā iti yā kācit iti sarvā lokaprasiddhā bhrāntiḥ satyamuktā bādhacintāyāṃ, vakṣyate ca pramāṇalakṣaṇe, kintu māyāpramātāramapekṣya; yatastasyaiva arthakriyāviṣayau saṃvādavisaṃvādau saṃbhavataḥ evamaikyaṃ nigamayya māheśvaryaṃ nigamayati sūtreṇa sa eva vimṛśattvena niyatena maheśvaraḥ vimarśa eva devasya śuddhe jñānakriye yataḥ avicchinnavimarśatvaṃ nāma yat vimṛśadrūpatvaṃ tata eva niyatam nahi asya prakāśalakṣaṇaṃ rūpaṃ nīlasukhādyuparāgarūapaṃ vā galvarkamaṇeriva avimṛṣṭaṃ jātucit bhavati, tena ananyonmukhatātmanā ānandarūpeṇa ahamiticamatkārātmanā mahānīśvaraḥ, yato devasya ete eva jñānakriye śuddhe pāramārthikyau yo'yaṃ vimarśo nāma uktanyāyāt iti svabhāvamavabhāsasya.......................... ityatra antare syādetat bhavatu nāma prakṛtau saṃvedanalakṣaṇaḥ prakāśaḥ, pratyaye tu kvipi bhāva eva abhidheyo, natu vimarśaḥ, tat kathamuktam prakṛtipratyayābhyām iti evaṃ manyatedhātunā tāvat saṃvedanaṃ jñānalakṣaṇamuktaṃ, ghañādayastu kriyāyāmeva vidhīyante, sā tu kriyā dharmāntareṇa siddhatākhyena bheditaiva bhāvapratyayavācyā siddhatāpratyavamarśayogyataiva- ayaṃ pākaḥ iti atra kevalaṃ pratyavamarśo bhavan na pākakriyāsvātmarūpaniveśī pramātustathāpratyavamarśodayāt, saṃvedane tu prakāśavapuṣi pratyavamṛśyatā bhavantī na anyāpekṣayā yuktā,- iti saṃvedanatādātmyavṛtti yat pratyavamṛśyamānatvaṃ, tadeva siddhatārūpapratyavamarśasvabhāve [rūpaṃ pratya svātantryeviśrāmyatīti ataśca saṃmelitau prakṛtipratyayau jñānakriyāvimarśalakṣaṇaṃ jaḍavailakṣaṇyāpādakaṃ [tmakaṃ rūpaṃ yasyāstādṛśīṃ paripūrṇalakṣaṇāmabhivyaṅktaḥ anusandhānātmanaḥ iti pramāsu svātantryaṃ darśitam asya iti paramātmanaḥ nanu evaṃ cit ityatra yadi jñānakriye praviṣṭe, tarhi jñānamityatrāpi prakṛtipratyayasadbhāvāt te praviṣṭe eva, tat kiṃ punaḥ kriyā iti adhikamabhidhīyate atra ucyate jñānamityapi iti satyamevamekākini api atra śabde iti apiśabdaḥ ucyate iti prakṛtipratyayabhāgadvayena prādhānyena iti yadyapi prakṛtipratyayau pratyayārthaṃ saha brūtaḥ iti, tathāpi tasya pratyayārthasya prakṛtyarthadharmatvena sphuraṇāt dharmasya dharmiṇamudrecayataḥ eva dharmatvāt dharmiṇi pratyayalakṣaṇe bodhabhāge sa dharmaḥ prādhānyamunmajjayati kriyeti apica iti caḥ samuccaye yatrāpi bodhabhāgābhidhāyakaṃ bhāgāntaraṃ nāsti, tatrāpi evamiti apiśabdaḥ ata eva pūrvatra ucyate iti uktam, iha tu ākṣipta iti ākṣepahetumāha anavabodhasya iti etadevaca yuktamiti darśayati vastu ekameva iti nanu vimarśaḥ kasmāt māheśvaryam āha āñjasyena iti ananyāpekṣatā hi vimarśaḥ, saivaca svatantratā nanu bodhasya vimarśo vyāpakaḥ svāmī, bodho hi vimarśaṃ na vyabhicarati na tyajati kadācit, tatastasya avyabhicaraṇe karmatāyāṃ vācyāyāṃ kathaṃ kartṛtā uktā,- ityāśaṅkya samavyāptikayoritthamabhidhāne'pi na doṣaḥ,- iti brūte bodhasya avyabhicaraṇīyo'pi vimarśaḥ sadā iti bodhasya vimarśo'vyabhicaraṇīyaḥ, sa cāpi bodho'vyabhicaraṇīyaḥ sāmarthyāt vimarśasya, tasmādasya avyabhicāriṇo vimarśasya api kartṛtā na na yuktā samavyāptikatve hetumāha avyabhicāravattvāt iti paraspareṇeti yāvat evaṃ kartṛtāmupapādya hetūktiprasaṅgasmṛtena vyutpattyantareṇa yojayati tadāpi iti avyabhicāravattvaṃ yaduktaṃ, tato'pi hetormatvarthīyapratyayopapatteryujyate eva itthamabhidhānam nanu ātmamātravimarśo'sāvahamiti, tatra bhāvanirbharatā na chunk-v3-p-tattva-caturtho-close-k1-3-v4.text: atha caturtho vimarśaḥ prasṛtamanuttararūpādānandādikrameṇa viśvamadaḥ sarvāmṛtadharamantarbahiśca visṛjantamabhivande jñānakriyādhikārayugalena tattvārthasaṅgrahasahitena svaprakāśe'pi tattve yuktyupabṛṃhite nirūpite svataḥ ityaṃśaḥ pūritaḥ āgamādhikāreṇa, tameva arthamupodbalayatā śāstrataḥ iti ayam śāstradṛṣṭirapi tatprasiddhaguruparamparopadeśena samyagāgamatvaṃ neyā yathā uktaṃ prāk śāmbhavanītyādīnāmapi ityādi tata eva paramahadantarāladivyadivyādivyādivyasambandhamanādṛtya sbuddhipustakamātraśaraṇā viḍambitā ityāśayena pustakādhītavidyāśca gurukramavivarjitāḥ ācaranto diśantaśca pacyante narake ciram yātanārājarājānāṃ te bhoktāro vininditāḥ tasmādgurukramāyātaṃ diśanneti paraṃ śivam iti uktam tato gurutaḥ iti ayaṃ tṛtīyaḥ aṃśaḥ pūrayitavyaḥ uktaṃ hi śrīkiraṇāyāṃ ---------------------------gurutaḥ śāstrataḥ svataḥ iti tamaṃśaṃ pūrayituṃ ślokatrayeṇa prakārāntaramāha tatra prathamaślokena svaguruparvakramaṃ vadannādiśrīkaṇṭhanāthāt pravṛttimasya darśayati upadeśasya apūrvatvena aprayāsakāritvena avaśyopadeśyatāṃ ca dvitīyena abhijñānaprakaṭanātmanā upadeśaḥ sato'pi asatkalpasya anuprāṇakaḥ iti tatra ādaraḥ kartavyaḥ iti darśitam tṛtīyena vyākhyānaśravaṇacintanābhyasanasāphalyasiddhaye svakapūrvaguruvandanamavaśyaṃ kartavyamiti śikṣayā pravṛttaśiṣyānugrahāya svātmano gurutve yogyatābhidhānāya kīrtanīyo gurorvargaḥ śāstrārthasya prasiddhaye itinayaṃ pālayituṃ pituralaukikavastuviṣayaprasiddhyabhidhānena upakārāya prasiddho diṣṭe lokaḥ pravartate iti lokasya apravṛttasya pravartanādvāreṇa ca anugrahāya ca svātmano vaṃśapradarśanapūrvakanāmaprakaṭīkaraṇapuraḥsaramadhikāraprayoja- nasambandhābhidheyābhidhānānāṃ nigamanamiti prakaraṇārthaḥ pratiślokaṃ tu artho nirūpaṇīyaḥ saca spaṣṭa eva, vṛttivivṛtyośca nirūpitaḥ yattu kiñcit kiñcidaspaṣṭamatra, tadeva vimṛśyate iti prakaṭito mayā sughaṭa eṣa mārgo navo mahāgurubhirucyate sma śivadṛṣṭiśāstre yathā tadatra nidadhatpadaṃ bhuvanakartṛtāmātmano vibhāvya śivatāmayīmaniśamāviśansidhyati ata eva iti yataḥ pratyabhijñāmātrāt mokṣaḥ, tata eva yamaniyamādikleśayogo'nupayoga eva atra aspaṣṭatvāt iti sphuṭopāyamanāyāsamanārambhaṃ mahāphalam śrotumicchāmi deveśa yogaṃ yogavidāṃ vara iti prāṇāyāmādikairaṅgairyogāḥ syuḥ kṛtrimā yataḥ tena nākṛtakasyāsya kalāmarghanti ṣoḍaśīm ityādi ca yadapi rahasyāgameṣu nirūpitam, tathā vispaṣṭatvena na uktaṃ garbhīkṛtya tu nirūpitaṃ nacaitadaprasannena śaṅkareṇopadiśyate kathañcidupalabdhe'pi vāsanā na prajāyate vāsanāmātralābhe'pi yo'pramatto na jāyate tamanityeṣu bhogeṣu yojayanti vinyāyakāḥ iti yadi ahaṃ paramaśivaḥ sarvajñasarvakartṛtvāt, tarhi kimiti na śatrūnsarvān sapadi grase ityādirmāyīye dehādāvanabhyāsena vibhavecchāmayo hi paramo vighnaḥ sa etacchāstrārthapariśīlanena nivartate loke mokṣopāyatvena na pratītāḥ, nañabhāve tu lokaprasiddhā ye jñānakriyādayastairiti vyākhyā prathamaṃ pādaṃ vyākhyāya dvitīyaṃ vyācaṣṭe eṣa ca ityādinā anāviṣṭa ityantena ityatra anupraveśaḥ uktaḥ śaśvat ityādiḥ sarvo ityatra śivapada ityādinā svātmani māyāmohasaṃskārakaluṣasādhaka- vargābhilaṣitocitavibhūtyanāsaṅgena samyaktattvadarśitayā kṛtakṛtyatve jñānakriyayoḥ pariśeṣaviśeṣatvān parānugrahatantratā sakalalokalo- canatāṃ prapannena avalokatvena prasiddhiparyavasānaṃ nāma pūrvoktagurulakṣaṇam śivadṛṣṭi iti tadgatamāśrīkaṇṭhanāthāt guruparvakramaṃ sūcayati tatrahi śrīśrīkaṇṭhanāthaḥ śāsane samutsanne śrīdurvāsomuniṃ tadavatāraṇāya dideśa, so'pi śrītryambakādityaṃ traiyambakākhye lokaprasiddhyā tairimbābhidhāne gurusantāne pravartayitāraṃ mānasaṃ sasarja,-ityādi vitatya uktam śrīkaṇṭhanāthaśca adhigatatattvaḥ śrīmadanantanāthāt, so'pi śrībhagavacchaktitaḥ ityādi āgameṣu nirūpitamiti saṃpūrṇo guruparvakramaḥ uktaḥ samūḍhaḥ iti prabodhitaḥ, pakvacandanādisaṃskārasthirīkṛtasaurabhaśca ghanasāraḥ karpūram aṣṭādaśabhujādyākārasākṣātkaraṇabhrāntirvikatthano'yamadyāpi atattvajño'yamanupayoginirūpaṇarasiko'yamitica pratītiphalā mā bhūdityāśayena āha antaḥkṛta iti citrakarmaṇaḥ kva prakṛte upayogaḥ āha tajjñānasya eva aiśvaryajñānasya adhikālaukikavastuprāptau mūḍhānāṃ dṛḍhapratyayatā bhavatīti dvitīyamardhaṃ vivṛṇoti īśvara ityādinā anena hetutṛtīyāntena padena tat iti sautraṃ tasmādityarthaṃ vivṛtavān --------------------jīvanmukto na saṃśayaḥ ityādiṣu āgamasthāneṣu niyamārthavyākhyānāya vṛttau yaḥ evakāraḥ, taṃ vyācaṣṭe dehapātāt ityādinā adbhutatamatvamapi ca evakāreṇa sūcitamasya upadeśasya dehapātādekabhaviko mokṣaḥ itihi etadeva tāvadadbhutam ihaikabhaviko mokṣa eṣa tāvat parīkṣyatām anekabhaviko mokṣaḥ paścātsa ca gamiṣyati iti hi paramakṛpālunā bhagavatā āgamagranthena nirūpitamadbhutatvam idaṃ tu adbhutatamaṃ yatkila jīvanneva mukta iti taistairapyupayācitairupanatastanvyāḥ sthito'pyantike kānto lokasamāna evamaparijñāto na rantuṃ yathā lokasyaiṣa tathānavekṣitaguṇaḥ svātmāpi viśveśvaro naivālaṃ nijavaibhavāya tadiyaṃ tatpratyabhijñoditā upayācitaiḥ iti devatāprārthanadūtīpreṣaṇātmāvasthānivedanābhiḥ tanvyāḥ iti virahakṛśāyāḥ na rantumalam iti saṃbandhaḥ pratyabhijñānamātrādānandalābhaḥ, pariśīlanāt tu saṃbhogasahasraprāptiriti tulyamubhayatra vastuviśeṣa iti vastuni arthakriyālābhe kānte ca iti pūrvadṛṣṭe'pi mohātpūrvamavijñāte iti bhāvaḥ yadvā iti nirbhāte api anirbhātakalpatvaṃ, tato dṛḍhaniścaye tathābhimāna iti ubhayatra api tulyamiti yāvat ekatā prakāśātmā iti so'yaṃ iti hi atrāpi tattvedantayorekīkaraṇaṃ prakāśanam, ihāpi īśvaratāhantayorityarthaḥ āśrayaucitya iti dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikarūpau yāvāśrayau, tadaucityādeva tadbalānīto viśeṣo bhūṣaṇam, anyathāhi aikyameva syāt, na sādṛśyam janasyāyatnasiddhyarthamudayākarasūnunā īśvarapratyabhijñeyamutpalenopapāditā yaḥ kaścit jananadharmā, tasya ataḥ siddhiḥ; natu atra jātyācārādau bharaḥ iti sarvānugrāhakatvamuktam etacca prārambhe eva asmābhirvitatam tato'pi iti yaśaḥsamucitena phalena pituryogāt asya iti kartuḥ anena sarvataḥ kṛtakṛtyatvaṃ darśitam,-iti śivam vivṛtikāraḥ saṃkṣipya sarvamāha ittham ityādiślokaiḥ anena asmaduktena īśvaratāprakāreṇa yā susaṃvittiḥ sthitā, tām lāṭa ityādinā pūrvaṃ śuddhavaṃśajanmano dvitīye vāgīśvarīgarbhajanmani kṛte pūrṇaṃ dvijatvaṃ bhavatīti antaḥprakṛtiḥ iti amātyasuhṛtprāyaḥ karkābhidhānaḥ iti yadiyaṃ karkasaṃgrahādiśāstram janmamātre carame'bhimānaḥ iti darśayati tryambaka iti tisro devyo yadā iti śaktitrayaparipūrṇatryambakadāsyalakṣmīyogāt pūrvoktamitātmatāguṇīkaraṇatadrūpatonmajjanasamāveśāt taddāsaḥ kṛtakṛtyatvena sābhimāno'smi bhoga ityādi viśveśvarasya pratyabhijñāmṛtasya ca viśeṣaṇam asya upādeyatāmāha prāyeṇa ityādinā kheṭapālācāryaprabhṛtayo dvaitaprādhānyamaśiśriyan, tadanusāriṇo'pi anye tathaiva avidyayā iti anirvācyarūpayā ayaṃ brahmavādo'pi na ekāntavādo, na niścitādvayavādaḥ iti mataṃ na viśadamiti sambandhaḥ ātmā īśvaro nāsti teṣāṃ yo vastuto'sti, santānāntaraṃ ca asti yat vastuto nāsti,-iti avasanna iti upāyalābhābhāvāt asmiṃstu sati āgameṣu dvaitavyākhyānamapāsya brahmavāde avidyāṃ māyāśaktīkṛtya vijñānādvayamātmeśvarābhiprāyeṇa nirūpya sidhyati eva jano yathā pūrvamuktamiti darśayati asminnevam iti pārameśvareṣu tāvadāgameṣu śaivavaiṣṇavarahasyeṣu vedānteṣu ca spaṣṭa eva ukto'yamasmadukto'rthaḥ tadanusāriṇā eva sugatena uktaṃ cittamātramidaṃ yaduta traidhātukam iti tadatra vivaraṇakārairdurabhiniveśavaśena vipratārito janaḥ idameva tu tattvamiti tu tātparyam ata eva prathāto'khilagrahaṇena idamāha-sakalo lokaḥ sakalaṃ ca śāstramasmābhiryadyapi na avalokyate, tathāpi yatkiñcit vastu vā, vikalpitaṃ vā; tat sarvaṃ prathamānameva sat bhavati prathamānatā ca prathārūpāt bhagavataḥ paramaśivādanatirekiṇī,-iti sa eva paryantopāsanīyaḥ paramaśivaḥ upāsitaḥ kalpate paramaśivāya,-iti śivam bhaṭṭātriguptakulajātavarāhagupta- janmābhavat cukhulakaḥ śivamārganiṣṭhaḥ śrībhūtirājavadanoditaśambhuśāstra- tattvāṃśuśātitasamastabhavāndhakāraḥ tajjanmadehapadabhāk padavākyamāna- saṃskārasaṃskṛtamatiḥ parameśaśakteḥ sāmarthyataḥ śivapadāmbujabhaktibhāgī dārātmajaprabhṛtibandhukathāmanāptaḥ nānāgurupravarapādanipātajāta- saṃvitsaroruhavikāsaniveśitaśrīḥ śrīśāstrakṛddhaṭitalakṣmaṇaguptapāda- satyopadarśitaśivādvayavādadṛptaḥ sarvānyaśāsanakathāḥ kalaviṅkakeli- kalpāḥ paraṃ prakalayanniha śāstrasāre ājñāmalaṅghyaphaladāṃ gurunāthapāda- nityārcanasmaraṇayogakṛtāmavāpya śrīśāmbhavādvayapade janatāṃ niyoktu- mabhyuditaḥ sakalasaṃpadudāravṛttau ṭīkāvimarśamakarollaghunā nayena spaṣṭena cābhinavaguptapadapratiṣṭhaḥ nādātuṃ naca dātumeṣa sulabhaḥ kiṃ kṛtyametāvate- tyevaṃ tarkayatā janena śakalīkṛtyātha yadgṛhyase māṇikyācala candrakīrtiracalā sā te jagadvyāpinī lokasyaiva mitopayogarasikasyaiṣā punaḥ khaṇḍanā saṅkocya niñcidiha kiñcidatha prasārya prakṣipya kiñcidiva kiñcidathāpyapāsya vidvāñjano bhavatu saṃprati śāstrakṛcca samyakpracāraṇavidhiḥ sahi janma tasya kalpāntāmbunidheḥ pracaṇḍapavanaprakṣobhitaurvānala- vikāsaṃ vaikharyāṃ ca prakaṭapadavīṃ śrotravṛttiṃ prayātu viśrāntā cedabhinavamatistadvimarśinyathānta- statsāphalyaṃ bhajati nitarāmīśvarapratyabhijñā pāṣāṇān prati vaktu kaḥ śṛṇuta bho yuṣmān bruve jaṅgamāḥ śayyotthāyamanarthamarthasaraṇe ko'yaṃ vṛthaivodyamaḥ saṃviddhāmani śāmbhave viśatha cetkālīyamekaṃ lavaṃ kiṃ kiṃ varṇanikābhirābhirabhitaḥ satyaṃ svayaṃ jñāsyatha paricinuta tadenāmīśvarapratyabhijñāṃ dahata hṛdi niviṣṭaṃ vāsanācakravālam jvaladanalaśikhāntarlelihānāraṇeya- sthiraparicayabhāk kiṃ sūtaye bījapuñjaḥ vākyapramāṇapadatattvasadāgamārthāḥ svātmopayogamamutaḥ yāvānātmāvaraṇavidhaye kalpate ko'pi kalpa- stāvānātmaprakaṭanavidhau nīta evopayogam yena spaṣṭaṃ paramagurave tīvrakāruṇyapūrṇa- śrīśarvāṇīdayitasatatāveśabhāje namo'smai iti navatitame'smin
